The geometry is exact; the business meaning needs your local knowledge. An area figure is the ceiling of a commitment, not a forecast of orders.
Why does one extra mile matter so much?
Area grows with the square of the radius. The ring between 4 and 5 miles (28.3 mi²) is larger than the entire 3-mile disc (28.27 mi²) — outer rings are where delivery economics go to die.
Radius or travel time — which should define a zone?
Time, ideally: customers experience minutes, not miles. Use this area for capacity, and the Drive Time Map for the zone's real shape.
Can I use the result for professional work?
For planning and internal decisions, yes. Published delivery promises should also survive a road check of the zone's awkward corners.
Yes — enter the radius in kilometres and read km² directly; a 5 km radius is 78.54 km², the same digits as 5 miles in mi², which is the square law's party trick.
Should the zone shrink at busy times?
Some operators do exactly that, because the commitment is area × demand density. This calculator prices the geometry of the smaller ring before the policy changes.
Why do platforms draw zones as polygons?
To cut the unprofitable corners off the circle. The area difference between their polygon and your radius's disc is the business you are declining or accepting.
